contributionFocus: Inject time, storage, events or network where used; use repeatable local fixtures and show that two isolated runs agree.

tests.description: Updating id=2 applies updates and gives a new object reference for record 2
tests.input: id=2, updates={ name: "Beta Updated", status: "active", count: 99 }
tests.expected: Record id=2 updated with new fields and timestamp; new array reference
tests.actual: Record 2 updated: name="Beta Updated", status="active", count=99

tests.description: Records not matching the target ID preserve original memory references
tests.input: id=2, check references for id=1 and id=3
tests.actual: Both unaffected object references strictly identical (===)

tests.description: Original input array items remain completely unchanged after operation
tests.input: Inspect original fixture after updateItemById call

tests.description: Updating a nonexistent ID leaves contents equivalent and original items untouched
tests.expected: Contents equivalent to original array; all element references retained
tests.actual: Result array deep equals original fixture; all element references identical

tests.description: Two isolated runs with deterministic fixture and injected clock produce identical output
tests.input: Two isolated runs on separate deterministic fixtures with mockClock

tests.description: Injected clock, storage, and event callbacks execute predictably
tests.input: Injected clock, storage mock, onEvent handler
tests.expected: Event emitted with type ITEM_UPDATED; storage.save called with result

tests.description: Rejects invalid non-array input with a TypeError
tests.expected: TypeError: First argument must be an array
